Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Hiro (serving runtime) and Neha (security) who will lead the session.

High-level answers so we can be efficient in the doc/meeting:

1) Trust domains: we generally recommend separate SPIFFE-style identities for control plane components (control.redwood.acme) and data-plane nodes (data.redwood.acme). Separate trust domains allow independent rotation windows and least-privilege ACLs.

2) TLS termination: preferred pattern is TLS termination at the control-plane ingress for management/control APIs (API front-door), and mutual TLS between control-plane and data-plane (i.e., control authenticates workers with mTLS). For customer-facing inference traffic you can choose edge termination (external load balancer) + mTLS internally depending on latency/SLOs.

3) Certificate issuance + KMS: short-lived certs (1-7 day) issued by Vault with a signing backend backed by your KMS is a good model. Redwood can integrate with Vault using a pull model for node bootstrap and a rotation webhook for control-plane cert refresh.

4) Observability: ensure that tracing headers are forwarded at the proxy boundary when TLS is terminated at the edge. When mTLS is end-to-end, you should map SPIFFE IDs to service labels in tracing to preserve identity in traces.

Action items:
- Hiro: prepare a 1-page reference diagram and sequence describing handshake/rotation flow (control <-> data).
- Neha: prepare a short checklist for KMS/Vault integration and recommended rotation cadence (include audit log requirements).
- Jasmine: schedule 45-min sync Tue 2027-08-10 09:00 PST (proposed) — ping if that doesn't work.

Attached: I included our quick one-page template (cert-rotation-proposal-v1.xlsx) and I'll share the updated drawio in the sync.

Jasmine / Daniel — quick technical notes ahead of the meeting. Quoting Jasmine's summary below for context.

On Tue, 3 Aug 2027 at 09:04, jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 1) Trust domains: we generally recommend separate SPIFFE-style identities for control plane components (control.redwood.acme) and data-plane nodes (data.redwood.acme).

Notes:
- Control-plane endpoints (API, scheduler, admin): terminate TLS at the control-plane ingress (front proxy) and enforce client mTLS for downstream requests from data-plane when sending control signals. This keeps management interfaces tightly controlled.
- Data-plane (worker/serving VMs): workers should present short-lived certs with SPIFFE SANs; enforce mTLS on the worker side to validate control plane connections.
- SNI + ALPN: use SNI routing at the front proxy so a single LB can multiplex control vs inference endpoints; ALPN can help with protocol negotiation for tracing-aware proxies.
- Cert rotation: propose staggered rotation windows (control-plane rotates every 7 days, data-plane rolling rotation over 2 days) to avoid mass reboots and to maintain cache consistency for KV caches.
- Bootstrap: use Vault agent bootstrap on node init to request node certs; store CA signing keys in Vault HSM mode (no long-lived private key on hosts).

Observability caveats:
- When TLS is terminated at an external edge, ensure the proxy preserves x-request-id/x-trace headers in the decrypted path and re-injects them when re-mTLS to the internal services.

I'll attach a concise sequence diagram in the meeting (control->vault->node->control). For the meeting, I suggest we walk the handshake sequence and a failure/recovery play (what happens if Vault is unavailable during rotation).
